sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let’s make your code smarter! Today, you’ll learn how to make decisions in Java using `if` statements.

• How to check conditions and run code only when they’re true
• Simple syntax that’s easy to remember
• Real examples you can try right now

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you’re a traffic light. 
- **Green light?** Cars go (`if` condition is true → run code).
- **Red light?** Cars stop (`if` condition is false → skip code).

`if` statements work the same way! They let your program choose what to do based on conditions.

• **Basic structure**: `if (condition) { do this }`
• **Example**: `if (age >= 18) { System.out.println("You can vote!"); }`
• **Key idea**: The code inside `{}` only runs if the condition is `true`.

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: An if statement executes its body only when the condition evaluates to true
The condition must be a boolean expression enclosed in parentheses
Use braces {} for the body even with a single statement to avoid errors
If the condition is false, the body is skipped and execution continues after it
Nested if statements can be used but should be kept simple for readability

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: `if` statements let your code make decisions. Conditions must evaluate to `true` or `false`. Practice with real examples (like checking grades or ages)

questions.question: What is the correct syntax for an if statement in Java?
questions.explanation: Java requires the condition of an if statement to be enclosed in parentheses: if (condition) { statements; }. This is mandatory syntax.

questions.question: What happens if the condition in an if statement is false?
options: The code inside the if block is skipped
questions.explanation: If the condition in an if statement evaluates to false, the code inside the if block is simply skipped, and execution continues with the next statement after the if block.
